question: What protective claim is made about poison with respect to the body, even in the case of being bitten by great serpents?
premises: A negation states that poison does not enter the body.
This is claimed even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body under the condition presupposed by this claim.
uncertainties: The condition that produces this protection is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
